criteria.rationale: Checked L1 and the spec's risk statement against the code. Verified: directories are created with exclusive Mkdir (review_dispatch.go:2166), the fallback takes the new attempt's own name exclusively, and an lstat error counts as held. L1's three guards remain untested, accepted by the spec; the untested recorded-continuation returns fall outside it (N2). That a resumed session tolerates a moved checkout is an unverified assumption (N5).
Read the CLI consumers of resume and handoff plans (delegate.go, delegate_handoff.go); signatures changed only inside package pose. The mismatched-continuation behaviour is reported as N1.
A moved checkout is recorded in safety.limitations with its reason and the thread reason names the held path; the minor empty-path race is N6.

The design assessment observed no structural deltas, so there is nothing to map. Exclusive directory creation as the lock, claim-file gating of ledger reads, and a fallback to the attempt's own directory address the causes behind R1 to R4; the gap in the R1 result selection is N1.

Compared the ten files of change set cs-61d69e9d2ff2 with the spec's artifacts and R1 to R6; no unrelated behaviour was found in them. Other commits in the range belong to other specs. Incomplete delivery is N2.

Examined path derivation and directory creation: the recorded runtime name is bounded by a regular expression, creation is exclusive, nothing removes a directory the dispatch did not create, and session reading is unchanged. The new records include a local temporary path, which R4 asks for. The old-path reference of a resumed session is reported in N5.

The change is small and local with no new abstraction beyond an error type carrying the recorded run. A smaller alternative for the late-held path (open a new session) would need replanning after attempt reservation; the chosen fallback is proportionate while the run records the move. It would be invalidated if resumed agents depended on the old absolute path.

findings.action: awaitContinuationClaim returns any recorded continuation without checking its kind or agent. A resume that loses the race to a completed handoff gets that handoff run as its own successful result (review_dispatch.go:761-763; PlanReviewResume at review_run_continuity.go:440-444, returned by the replan at review_dispatch.go:740-741), bypassing the 'handed off; it is not resumed' refusal at review_run_continuity.go:423-424. A handoff that loses inside takeContinuationRuntimeDir to a resume or to another agent's handoff also returns that run as success instead of 'already continued' (delegation_handoff.go:339-342), contrary to R1. Established by code reading.

R6 is traced satisfied but is not delivered: no test makes the exclusive take refuse after a successful replan (review_dispatch.go:764-766 uncovered; the dispatch-beside-a-directory test is refused earlier by the replan), none covers the claim-failure removal (769-771 uncovered), and Known gaps admits the random-name resume and the handoff pending branch are missing. R1's recorded-continuation returns (review_dispatch.go:761-763 and the existing return of awaitContinuationClaim, review_run_continuity.go:440-445, delegation_handoff.go:357-361) are also uncovered by the focused tests and are outside L1, which names only the claim-publication conflict.

A cancelled wait returns (nil,nil), so takeContinuationRuntimeDir returns the 'runtime directory already exists ... remove it' error instead of the context error, advising removal of a directory another resume may hold. The waits reached through replanContinuation use context.Background() (review_run_continuity.go:435, delegation_handoff.go:352), so cancellation is not honoured there for up to about two seconds.

After a claim conflict, a replan that refuses because the winner was a different continuation (resume lost to a handoff, or handoff lost to another agent) is discarded and the raw publication conflict is returned instead of the 'already continued' or 'handed off' answer.

The manual (both locales) says a held previous checkout path opens a new session, but a path taken after the plan keeps the continued session and moves its checkout (review_dispatch.go:848-858); the resumed session may still refer to the old path, which can hold another live run's checkout. The manual does not describe this, and spec section 5 records no decision for this or for returning recorded continuations, although its Constraints require one when a fix changes an answer.

previousRoundCheckoutHeld is evaluated twice; if the holder removes the directory between line 695 and line 701 the recorded reason is 'checkout path  is still in use' with no path. A path that only failed lstat is also reported as still in use.
